cells.tense: You're in the middle of putting something down, and your hands are open while you do it.
cells.ask: As one ending settles, offer care to whatever is quietly starting — a little time, a little attention, no pushing.
cells.core: You're in the middle of putting something down, and your hands are open while you do it. What you're releasing is finished, and you can feel that it's finished. Nothing is being torn away — you open a hand and it's lighter. When an ending arrives here, you let it arrive, and you don't spend the next month arguing with it; that's the whole of what makes this look easy from the outside. People can tell, because you're not braced against the loss. You're standing in the room the ending cleared. There's a next thing taking root near where the old one stood, and it doesn't need to be hurried, only noticed. Give it what it actually asks for and no more, and you'll be tending it without spending yourself on it.
cells.sheetLine: You're letting go because it's finished, not because you lost.
cells.place: the clearing where something has run its course

cells.tense: Somewhere ahead of here you've already decided this is over, and you're living out of that ending before it has arrived.
cells.ask: Pick one small practice and keep it on an ordinary day — a set time, a short stretch, the same few minutes — and let that steadiness hold you instead of the next big gesture.
cells.core: Somewhere ahead of here you've already decided this is over, and you're living out of that ending before it has arrived. You keep finishing things early — whatever is still half-alive gets declared done, and the letting go turns into something you do to show you're above it. It can look noble from the outside, and it costs you everything that was still coming. Ended one at a time, each when it's actually finished, this reads as patience instead of severity. That kind of patience isn't dramatic. It's a small practice kept faithfully — a set time, a short stretch, the same few minutes — tending what you care about instead of racing the end.
cells.sheetLine: You're ending things ahead of their time and calling it strength.

cells.tense: The door swung shut and you're still standing at it, holding it closed with both hands.
cells.ask: Let one ending be carried by something sturdier than your own grip — give yourself a structure that holds the weight while you rest, once today, in a form you can touch.
cells.core: The door swung shut and you're still standing at it, holding it closed with both hands. You've been keeping something in place far past the point where it needed you. The work of it has become the day, and underneath the effort you're tired in a way sleep doesn't touch. Set down, this looks like trusting a thing to stay where it is without your arms around it. That trust doesn't come from trying harder to relax. It comes from giving your grip a stand-in — a routine, a person, a place where the weight rests on its own. Let something else hold the door, once today, and see that it stays shut without you.
cells.sheetLine: You're exhausted from holding shut what's already closed.
cells.place: the clearing where something has run its course

cells.tense: You're describing this stretch as still in play, while your hands have already let go of something.
cells.ask: Lend care to one thing that's quietly growing near you — a person, a project, a small daily practice — as caring, not as a chore on a list.
cells.core: You're describing this stretch as still in play, while your hands have already let go of something. The release happened; you keep narrating the hold. Meanwhile something new has come up beside the old place, and you've been tending it — watering it, making room — without counting it as anything. Tending it at the pace it actually grows, without standing over it with a schedule, is the whole of the work, and you've been doing it already, unnamed. It doesn't need a declaration or a plan. It needs to be recognized as yours, the way you'd notice you've been caring for a plant that's already in bloom.
cells.sheetLine: You've already let go — you just haven't told yourself yet.
